blogs.title: Why AI Models 'Collapse' During Training—and How GSPO Fixes It
blogs.description: Ever wonder why training massive AI models can sometimes result in a total breakdown of intelligence? This post dives into the 'catastrophic collapse' seen in current reinforcement learning algorithms like GRPO. We'll explain how tiny errors at the individual token level snowball into massive training noise and how the new Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) provides a stable foundation for the next generation of LLMs.

blogs.title: The Power of the Whole: Why Sequence-Level Logic is the Future of RL
blogs.description: In AI training, there's a fundamental rule: the unit of optimization should match the unit of reward. If you reward a model for a whole sentence, why are we still training it one word at a time? This blog explores the core innovation of GSPO—shifting from token-level to sequence-level importance ratios—and how this elegant shift allows models like Qwen3 to achieve superior performance with better efficiency.

blogs.title: Simplifying the Giants: How GSPO Unlocks Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Models
blogs.description: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are the heavy hitters of the AI world, but they are notoriously difficult to train using standard reinforcement learning due to 'expert volatility.' We explore how GSPO solves this headache by removing the need for complex workarounds like 'Routing Replay,' allowing developers to train massive, sparse models more simply and effectively than ever before.

blogs.title: Bridging the Gap: Making AI Infrastructure Easier to Build
blogs.description: One of the biggest headaches in AI engineering is the precision discrepancy between training engines (like Megatron) and inference engines (like vLLM). This post explains how GSPO's sequence-level approach is inherently more tolerant of these differences, potentially simplifying the entire RL infrastructure and making it easier for developers to deploy large-scale models.
